selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: After leaving the gathering of the prophets, where was the traveler invited next?
questions.answer: He was invited to the learning circle of deeply truthful and purified scholars who defend the message of the prophets with strong proof.

questions.question: What title is given to the scholars in this passage besides being learned?
questions.answer: They are described as purified and especially truthful people.

questions.question: What did the traveler witness inside their classroom?
questions.answer: He witnessed an immense body of gifted scholars proving the foundations of belief.

questions.question: Why is their agreement itself presented as evidence?
questions.answer: Because so many intelligent and insightful people, even with different abilities and perspectives, reached the same core truths.

questions.question: What does their unity in the foundations of belief show?
questions.answer: It shows that the basics of faith are strong, clear, and recognized by many trustworthy minds.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from this broad agreement?
questions.answer: It treats their unity as a major proof in itself.

questions.question: What comparison is used to explain the effect of denial?
questions.answer: It is compared to someone shutting his own eyes, which does not make day disappear except for himself.

questions.question: What is the main point of the day-and-night comparison?
questions.answer: Truth does not disappear when someone refuses to acknowledge it.

questions.question: What kind of power did the traveler feel in their classroom?
questions.answer: He felt an inner strength of faith and character that disbelief could not break.

questions.question: What does the final declaration say their agreement points to?
questions.answer: It points to Allah’s necessary existence in His unity.

questions.question: Why did the traveler enter the classroom of the purified scholars?
questions.answer: He had gained a high taste of truth through belief and wanted to continue learning from those who strongly confirmed the prophets’ message.

questions.question: What makes these scholars “original” and “exacting” in the passage?
questions.answer: They think deeply and carefully, and they build their conclusions with disciplined and rigorous proof.

questions.question: How are these scholars intellectually described in the passage?
questions.answer: They are described as profound, original, precise, and highly capable.

questions.question: Why is it important that they agreed even though they were not identical in viewpoint?
questions.answer: Their agreement shows that the truths of faith are not based on one narrow perspective but are recognized across different minds and approaches.

questions.question: Why is shared agreement among so many scholars treated as powerful evidence?
questions.answer: Because widespread agreement among capable and insightful experts strongly supports the truth of what they affirm.

questions.question: What personal quality supported each scholar’s conclusion?
questions.answer: Each one relied on a proof that was firm and certain.

questions.question: What effect had the scholars’ light had over time and place?
questions.answer: It had spread widely and continued to give light to a large part of the world for over a millennium.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the reach of the scholars’ light?
questions.answer: It says their light had illuminated half the earth.

questions.question: What kind of force did he discover among them?
questions.answer: He discovered a moral and spiritual force too strong to be shaken by all the deniers together.

questions.question: How are the proofs of the purified scholars described in the concluding line?
questions.answer: They are described as clear, verified, and united.

questions.question: What kind of “taste” did the traveler gain before reaching the scholars’ classroom?
questions.answer: He gained an elevated experience of truth that came from the strength of belief.

questions.question: What was the purpose of these scholars’ work?
questions.answer: Their purpose was to establish the truths of faith through powerful and decisive arguments.

questions.question: How strong were their proofs described to be?
questions.answer: Their arguments were presented as so deep and firm that they left no opening for doubt.

questions.question: What area of religion were they proving together?
questions.answer: They were proving the positive truths connected to faith, especially Allah’s existence and oneness.
